texts.preamble: Syed Javed Ali S/O Syed Hasan Ali vs State Of Mah., Thr Police Station ... on 12 June, 2019 Author: Manish Pitale Bench: Manish Pitale 1/3 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Nagpur Bench, Nagpur. Criminal Application (Aba) No.351 Of 2019 Syed Javed Ali Syed Hasan Ali-Vs.-State of Maharashtra ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Office notes, Office Memoranda of Coram, appearances, Court's orders Court's or Judge' or directions and Registrar's orders. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Mr.S.A.Mohta counsel for the applicant. Mr.V.P.Maldhure, App counsel for the respondent. Coram : Manish Pitale, J. Date : 12.06.2019.
texts.facts: 4. The applicant is one of the accused in First Information Report dated 1.6.2019 registered against him and two other persons for allegedly having committed offences under Sections 188, 272, 328 r/w Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code r/w Sec.26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(b)(e), 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. It is alleged that the co-accused persons were intercepted and found to be in possession of huge quantity of Guthkha, which is a prohibited item in the state of Maharashtra. It is alleged that said material recovered from the co- accused was found to be worth Rs. 1,884,400.00/- KAVITA 1-aba-351-19.odt and when enquiry was made with the co-accused they took name of the applicant as a person to whom the material belonged. On this basis, First Information Report was registered against all the accused persons including the applicant herein. on 12 June, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84251999/ 1 5.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel appearing for the applicant points out that Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not apply in the present case at all, because the ingredients of the said offence are not made out in the present case. Reliance is placed by the learned counsel for the applicant on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Joseph Kurian.. It is contended that the other offences are also not made out against the applicant and that other than the statement of the co-accused there appears nothing to connect the applicant with the alleged offence. The learned APP has opposed grant of such ad interim protection, contending that the judgment of Devision Bench of this Court covers the case against the applicant insofar as section 328 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned and it is further contended that custody of the applicant would be required to KAVITA 1-aba-351-19.odt enquire about the syndicate behind the manufacture, supply and transport of the aforesaid prohibited material.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel appearing for the applicant points out that Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not apply in the present case at all, because the ingredients of the said offence are not made out in the present case. It is contended that the other offences are also not made out against the applicant and that other than the statement of the co-accused there appears nothing to connect the applicant with the alleged offence.
